speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether the Support for Job Redesign programme is deployed to incentivise flexible work arrangements that mirror platform autonomy to attract platform workers back to traditional employment; and (b) if so, what results have been achieved through this programme.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Given the impact on the long-term career progression on workers who remain in platform work longer than intended, will the Ministry consider such a target to track the number of platform workers who transition back into full-time traditional employment every year, so as to better track the success of relevant initiatives and programmes to achieve that?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And secondly, given that platform work is often perceived to offer better pay and time flexibility than equivalent traditional jobs for workers of the same education levels, how is the Ministry of Manpower working with employers to make workplaces more attractive on these two aspects to incentivise platform workers to make the transition?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And what measurable results have been achieved to date?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: Platform workers may choose to do platform work for various reasons.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: For example, greater flexibility or control over when and how their work is being done.
